events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn by the author on 2024-01-17, conceding a miscomputed moat width in the key step.

events.what: Das preprints (arXiv:1908.10392, arXiv:1901.10016) on the moat problem and an extension; withdrawn in 2024-09-06 v2s stating the theorems were incorrect
events.credibility_reason: The author withdrew both, saying the theorems were incorrect; the 2024 revisions are withdrawal notices, not new mathematics (F7).

judgement.doubts: The Tsuchimura computational moat record (k=sqrt(36)) dates from 2004/2005 and is only instances/bound background. There is no post-snapshot event.

corrections.why: F6: the only event is the Stumpenhusen claim, which was posted 2024-01-16 and withdrawn 2024-01-17 because 'the width of the moat was not correctly computed'. That makes it knocked down, and it also predates the snapshot. It moved no bound. Nothing survives step 1, and the problem was not resolved before the snapshot, so the status is open. The record's own competing_reading already calls this 'the more defensible one'.
other: the summary says no post-2024-01-26 paper, announcement or computational record was found. The Das 2024 v2s only withdraw 2019 claims.
other: no event supports the status, so there is nobody to credit. The withdrawn claim stays in the record as evidence.
